page: The Amazon Web Services m7g.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the ARM-based AWS Graviton3 platform. Driven by ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture operating at 2.6 GHz, the system features 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of memory, providing an even 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, along with 32 MB of L3 cache and a 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not bundle local ephemeral storage, relying completely on remote EBS volumes for disk operations, and includes no hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight substantial parallel compute and memory throughput. The instance reaches a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 20,663.0, paired with an exceptional Clang software compilation score of 58,543.0 and strong multi-core stress-ng throughput of 97,878.33. Memory performance is similarly robust, demonstrating a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,151.64 alongside uncached read bandwidth of 253.34 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 121.49 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects average performance across Geekbench and compression tasks, indicating that throughput gains depend heavily on parallelized execution.

The physical-core design eliminates resource contention between virtual threads, offering consistent performance per core and high computational efficiency for large multithreaded deployments. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires architectural consideration when designing I/O-intensive pipelines, as all disk traffic routes through network-attached storage.

The m7g.16xlarge is best suited for horizontally scaled multi-threaded applications, including continuous integration build farms, distributed in-memory caching clusters like Redis, large-scale static web fleets, microservice orchestrations, and high-concurrency database workloads.
description: The Amazon Web Services m7g.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-V1 architecture running at 2.6 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It provisions 64 dedicated physical cores without multithreading, 256.0 GB of RAM at 4.0 GB per core, and a 30 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance lacks local ephemeral storage and GPU acceleration, directing all persistent storage workloads over the network. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate exceptional parallel processing and memory capabilities, achieving top-tier results in multi-core Clang compilation, top-tier PassMark memory scores, and strong throughput in Redis operations and static web serving. While single-thread benchmarks remain within average ranges, the dedicated-core topology ensures stable execution under concurrent loads, making the system appropriate for large microservice backends, CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed caching layers, and high-concurrency transactional database environments.
